experiment: core-theory red-team: does a developed ROP/JOP chain survive a morph cycle?
instrument: mtd chainsim (mtd_metrics/src/chainsim.rs), gadgets via unaligned iced-x86 decode, chains sampled uniformly from base gadget set

attacker_A_static_chain.model: hardcoded gadget offsets from cycle N fired unchanged at cycle N+1; viable iff ALL steps land at same offset with identical gadget text
attacker_A_static_chain.verdict: layout-shuffle morph annihilates stockpiled/developed chains (0/7000 across lengths); byte-level morph alone is insufficient (72.5% survive)

attacker_B_leak_and_rebase.model: runtime disclosure; re-derives each gadget by normalized semantic kind anywhere in the morphed image
attacker_B_leak_and_rebase.verdict: layout churn alone does NOT defeat per-target weaponized attackers: ~1/3 of short chains rebuildable. Cadence (attacker C) is the load-bearing variable against this class.

attacker_C_cadence_breakeven.model: P(success) = max(0, 1 - window/period), periodic morph, uniformly random attack phase
attacker_C_cadence_breakeven.verdict: morph defeats re-derivation only when the full attack window (disclose -> scan -> assemble -> deliver) approaches the morph period. Hourly cadence defeats >= hour-scale weaponization; seconds-scale automated attacks require seconds-scale cadence.

direct_attack_2026_07_27.note: NOT a simulation. A real ROP chain (ret-sled + attack_win) was built from base-ELF address intelligence, delivered via QEMU fw_cfg to a live kernel's planted stack-overflow serial/fw_cfg surface (attack_vulnerable_service), and executed under TCG. Verdicts are from serial logs; crashes corroborated by QEMU exception dumps.

same exploit bytes die against the morphed kernel — BLUE WINS
byte-level morphing does NOT stop the chain — binmorph alone is cosmetic, proven at execution level

soak_scaling_finding_2026_07_29.run: 1000-cycle duration soak: 243 consecutive ACCEPTED cycles (zero rejects, continuity boots=249, WAL checkpoint rotation fired live at ~boot 170 as designed) before the environment broke
soak_scaling_finding_2026_07_29.finding: UNBOUNDED SOURCE BLOAT: stack pads were injected per cycle but never stripped. Sources grew ~27x in 243 cycles (dns.rs 22KB→609KB, tls.rs 71KB→1.9MB). Past the threshold, syn's recursive AST visitors overflowed the default 8MB stack — the daemon died deterministically at cycle ~244 ('main has overflowed its stack'), and after restart every verify rejected (verifier subprocess also 8MB-limited). 757 consecutive REJECTED cycles followed, all from tooling choking on bloat, not from semantic failures.
fixes: diversifier stack_pad: strip-then-inject (strip_old_pads removes prior __cuttle_stack_pad_* before injecting fresh) + regression test: 50 apply cycles produce byte-identical size to 1 cycle
phase2_daemon: soak loop runs in a 256MB-stack thread (defense in depth for deep AST recursion)
soak_scaling_finding_2026_07_29.verdict: the soak did its job: found a scaling limit no short test could. Morph cycles are now provably size-bounded; the 243-cycle clean run + checkpoint rotation + this bug is the full duration-soak harvest. Moral for the paper: MTD factories need bounded-output invariants per cycle, not just correctness invariants.
